The *Gaṇikā Sutta* (Ud 6.8; PTS Ud 71) is a short discourse in the *Udāna* of the Khuddaka Nikāya. Set in the context of an incident where two rival factions come to blows over a courtesan (*gaṇikā*), the discourse culminates in an inspired utterance (*udāna*) spoken by the Buddha on the perils and suffering arising from sensual entanglements [SuttaCentral]. The sutta is also cited or cross-referenced in the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37, *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna*) [SuttaCentral]. Modern secondary literature surveyed in the research dossier mentions the term *gaṇikā* extensively in social and Vinaya contexts (such as the figures of Ambapālī and Sālavatī), but does not specifically examine this sutta.

The verse portion of the sutta finds direct cognates across Northern Buddhist verse collections. Curated parallels identify resembling verses in the twenty-seventh chapter (*Paśyavarga* / *Sight*) of the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (Uv 27 and UVS 27), the Tibetan translation (Uv Kg 27), and two Chinese translations of the *Udānavarga* (T 212.28 and T 213.27) [SuttaCentral].
